another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child(ren).

**How old is the child you're claiming for?** (Or if you have multiple children, please tell me about each one)

Please let me know:
- The child's name
- Their date of birth (or current age)

This will help me determine which eligibility pathway applies. Child Benefit generally depends on the child's age:
- **Under 16** years old: Generally eligible
- **16-19 years old**: Eligible if they're in full-time education or approved training
- **20 years or older**: Generally not eligible

Please provide these details so I can guide you through the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have a child, Alex, who's 6 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have **Alex, who is 6 years old**. Since Alex is under 16, this is a good starting point for eligibility.

Let me continue with the next step in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check a few things about Alex's circumstances.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

(This question helps us understand if there are any restrictions on eligibility due to employment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 6!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense – Alex is only 6 years old, so no work concerns there. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking whether Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit in their own right

(At 6 years old, this is unlikely, but I need to check for completeness.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't get any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

At 6 years old, this is very unlikely, but I need to confirm: Is Alex currently in any form of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 6!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're absolutely right! That's a straightforward no. Let me move forward to the next stage.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status, as this is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If not, please let me know your situation – for example:
- Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- Do you have pre-settled status and are you working, studying, or have sufficient resources?
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

The key question is: where do you normally reside, and what is your residency/immigration status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Thank you for clarifying that you're living abroad. To help determine if you might still be eligible for Child Benefit, I need to understand your specific situation better.

Can you tell me:

1. **Are you a Crown servant?** (For example, working for the UK government, Foreign Office, or in certain qualifying roles abroad)

2. **If not, do you have any connection to the EU Settlement Scheme?** For example:
   - Do you have settled status or pre-settled status?
   - Are you a family member of an EEA or Swiss national?

3. **Which country are you currently living in?** (This may also be relevant for Crown servant exceptions)

This information will help me determine if there's a pathway for you to remain eligible for Child Benefit while living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant, and I don't have any settled or pre-settled status. I'm just living abroad with my family.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Based on the information you've provided:

- You live abroad (outside the UK)
- You don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You're not a Crown servant

Unfortunately, this means you don't meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit eligibility. The rules require that you normally live in the UK to qualify, with only specific exceptions for:
- Those with settled/pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Crown servants living abroad in qualifying circumstances
- Those in certain other specific situations

Since none of these apply to your situation, I need to let you know:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Result: NOT ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit at this time because you don't meet the residency requirements.

**Why:**
- Child Benefit is only payable to those who normally live in the UK
- You currently live abroad and don't fall within any of the qualifying exceptions (settled/pre-settled EU status, Crown servant role, etc.)

**What this means:**
- Even though Alex would normally qualify as a child (being under 16 with no disqualifying circumstances), eligibility depends on the claimant (you) meeting the residency requirement

**Next steps:**
- If your situation changes and you move back to the UK in the future, you may become eligible at that point
- You could contact HMRC to discuss your specific circumstances: **0300 200 3100**
- Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility for more information

I'm sorry this wasn't the outcome you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help clarify about the eligibility rules?
